Definition: from G303 and G4727; to sigh deeply:--sigh deeply.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit over a generation seeking a sign, and said there would be no sign given to it. It is a deep sigh, from the spirit, not the lungs — the sigh of a man who sees the demand for proof and knows it will not believe anyway.
TheologicalSignificance: One deep sigh carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the sigh itself — Jesus sighing in His spirit at a generation that asks for a sign and will not believe one.
